11	/-!
12	# The Albanese universal property over an arbitrary base field
13	
14	`Albanese/AlbaneseJacobian.lean` instantiates Milne Proposition III.6.1 over an
15	**algebraically closed** field. This file removes that restriction, and states the result
16	in the shape the headline's fifth obligation `isAlbanese_pic0Et` (`Jacobian.lean`) asks
17	for: `IsAlbanese C P J`, over an arbitrary field `k`, for a given marked point.
18	
19	## What made this possible, and what it does *not* discharge
20	
21	The `k̄` restriction was never in Milne's argument. `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` proves
22	the factorisation in an arbitrary `CartesianMonoidalCategory`; the two geometric inputs it
23	consumes are Milne §I.1 Corollaries 1.4 and 1.2, and both are now available over an
24	arbitrary field (`Albanese/AVRigidityArbitraryField.lean`: commutativity is mathlib's
25	Stacks 0BFD, and pointed rigidity descends along `Over.pullback` because `IsMonHom` is a
26	pair of equations). So `isAlbanese_pic0Et`'s docstring pricing of the passage from `k̄` to
27	`k` as "the Galois-descent step of cluster `G`" overcharges for *this* step: no descent of
28	the universal property is needed, because the argument never needed the hypothesis.
29	
30	**This is not a discharge of `isAlbanese_pic0Et`, and the antecedents below are not
31	witnessed for any curve.** What is still owed, at any base field:
32	
33	1. `SymPowData C g` — the symmetric power `Sym^g C` with its symmetrisation projection,
34	   equivalently `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)`. This is the object the whole leg is
35	   blocked on (`AJC.albanese.symmetric`); the geometry is the cocycle agreement of the
36	   chart quotients plus `OrbitsInAffineOpen` for the curve;
37	2. `hdesc` — the descent datum, **for every target abelian variety `A`**. Over `k̄` this
38	   is supplied geometrically from a section of `f^{(g)}` over a dense open (Milne
39	   III.5.1(a) birationality, `exists_unique_descent_of_section`); that supply route is
40	   itself stated over `k̄` and is *not* transported here;
41	3. `aj`, `f`, `hf`, `haj0` — the Abel–Jacobi map and its symmetrisation. For the étale
42	   tower these must additionally be carried from `Pic0Scheme` to `Pic0SchemeEt`.
43	
44	Genus `0` is not a separate case *of this theorem* — it is covered by taking `g = 0` — but
45	the headline leaf also needs the genus-`0` instance of items 1–3, which is Mumford §4
46	rigidity and is not addressed here.
47	
48	## Main results
49	
50	* `albanese_up_of_symPowData_arbitraryField` — the unique-factorisation statement over an
51	  arbitrary field, matching `albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData_generic` with the
52	  `[IsAlgClosed]` binder deleted.
53	* `isAlbanese_of_symPowData_arbitraryField` — the same content packaged as `IsAlbanese`,
54	  i.e. in the shape `isAlbanese_pic0Et` and `JacobianWitness.isAlbaneseFor` consume. Note
55	  `IsAlbanese` quantifies over the target `A`, so the descent datum is required uniformly
56	  in `A`; that is visible in the hypothesis and is the honest form of the obligation.
57	
58	## References
59	
60	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1; §I.1 Corollaries 1.2 and 1.4.
61	-/

75	
76	Same statement as `albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData_generic`
77	(`Albanese/AlbaneseJacobian.lean`) with the `[IsAlgClosed kbar]` binder deleted: for any
78	object `C`, any `g`, any symmetric-power datum, and any two abelian varieties `J`, `A` over
79	`k`, a pointed `φ : C ⟶ A` factors uniquely through a pointed `aj : C ⟶ J` whose
80	symmetrisation is `f`, given the descent datum.
81	
82	The proof is the same call to `exists_unique_albanese_factorisation`; only the two rigidity
83	inputs change, to the arbitrary-field forms. -/
84	theorem albanese_up_of_symPowData_arbitraryField
85	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (g : ℕ)
86	    (D : SymPowData C g)
87	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g), permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
88	    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
89	    {J A : Over (Spec (.of k))}
90	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom]
91	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
92	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A])
93	    (aj : C ⟶ J) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)
94	    (hf : letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField J
95	      D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj)
96	    (haj0 : P0 ≫ aj = η[J])
97	    (hdesc : letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField A
98	      ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ) :
99	    ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ := by
100	  letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField J
101	  letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField A
102	  exact exists_unique_albanese_factorisation D f P0 i₀ hproj aj hf haj0 φ hφ
103	    (fun ψ hψ => isMonHom_of_pointed_arbitraryField ψ hψ) hdesc
104	
105	/-- **`IsAlbanese` over an arbitrary base field, from the symmetric power and the descent
106	datum.**
107	
108	This is the shape of the headline's fifth obligation `isAlbanese_pic0Et`: `J` *is* the
109	Albanese of the pointed curve `(C, P)`, over an arbitrary `k`, with no hypothesis on
110	`C(k)`.
111	
112	The universal morphism is the given `aj`. Because `IsAlbanese` quantifies over the target
113	`A`, the descent datum is needed **uniformly in `A`** — that is the `hdesc` binder, and it
114	is stated that way deliberately rather than for one `A`: a version taking the datum for a
115	single target would not produce `IsAlbanese`.
116	
117	What this reduces the obligation to is items 1–3 of the module header, none of which is
118	witnessed here for any curve. In particular no `SymPowData C g` exists in this development
119	for `g ≥ 2`, so this theorem has no inhabitant at a curve of genus `≥ 2` today; it is a
120	reduction of the leaf's *field* hypothesis, not of its content. -/
121	theorem isAlbanese_of_symPowData_arbitraryField
122	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
123	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
124	    (g : ℕ) (D : SymPowData C g)
125	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g), permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
126	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
127	    (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
128	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom]
129	    (aj : C ⟶ J) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)
130	    (hf : letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField J
131	      D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj)
132	    (haj0 : P ≫ aj = η[J])
133	    (hdesc : ∀ (A : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom]
134	      [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (φ : C ⟶ A),
135	      letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField A
136	      ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ) :
137	    IsAlbanese C P J := by
138	  refine ⟨aj, haj0, ?_⟩
139	  intro A _ _ _ _ φ hφ
140	  letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField J
141	  letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField A
142	  exact exists_unique_albanese_factorisation D f P i₀ hproj aj hf haj0 φ hφ
143	    (fun ψ hψ => isMonHom_of_pointed_arbitraryField ψ hψ) (hdesc A φ)
144	
145	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# The two rigidity corollaries over an arbitrary base field
11	
12	`Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean` proves Milne §I.1 Corollaries 1.4 (an abelian variety is
13	commutative) and 1.2 (a pointed morphism of abelian varieties is a homomorphism) on the
14	project's four-instance abelian-variety package, but over an **algebraically closed**
15	field: both rest on `RigidityLemma.lean`, whose engine binds `[IsAlgClosed kbar]`.
16	
17	This file removes that binder. Both corollaries hold over an arbitrary field `K`.
18	
19	## Why this matters, and what it does not buy
20	
21	The headline `picardJacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) is stated over an arbitrary field
22	with no rational-point hypothesis (owner decision, protection `I-0491`). Its fifth
23	obligation `isAlbanese_pic0Et` is the Albanese universal property there, and its docstring
24	prices the passage from `k̄` to `k` as "the Galois-descent step of cluster `G`".
25	
26	That price is too high for *this* part of the passage. The Albanese engine
27	(`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`) is already field-agnostic — it lives in an arbitrary
28	`CartesianMonoidalCategory` — and consumes exactly two geometric inputs, the two rigidity
29	corollaries. Both are available over `K`:
30	
31	* commutativity is *already* in mathlib over an arbitrary field
32	  (`isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`, Stacks 0BFD), which descends it
33	  from `K̄` internally; the project's own `IsAlgClosed` version is not needed at that
34	  strength, because `GeometricallyIntegral` synthesises from the four-instance package;
35	* pointed rigidity descends by the *same* argument, which is what this file supplies
36	  (`isMonHom_of_pointed_arbitraryField`). `IsMonHom` is a pair of equations, `Over.pullback`
37	  along `K → K̄` is faithful and monoidal, and the abelian-variety package is stable under
38	  that base change — so the `k̄` corollary applies upstairs and reflects back down.
39	
40	**What is still owed for `isAlbanese_pic0Et`, and this file does not touch any of it:**
41	the symmetric power `Sym^g C` (equivalently `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)`), Milne III.5.1(a)
42	birationality as a section over a dense open, the genus-`0` case, the basepoint condition,
43	and the transport of the Abel–Jacobi morphism to `Pic0SchemeEt`. Nothing here is a discharge
44	of the headline sorry; what it does is establish that the *field* is not among the reasons
45	that sorry is open.
46	
47	## Main results
48	
49	* `isMonHom_of_pointed_arbitraryField` — Milne I.1.2 over an arbitrary field.
50	* `isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField` — Milne I.1.4 over an arbitrary field, recorded
51	  here so the pair is available together (the proof is mathlib's 0BFD plus one instance).
52	-/
53	
54	set_option autoImplicit false
55	
56	universe u
57	
58	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
59	open scoped CategoryTheory.Obj
60	
61	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
62	
63	variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
64	
65	/-- **Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.4 over an arbitrary field: an abelian variety is
66	commutative.**
67	
68	Same conclusion as `isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package` with the `[IsAlgClosed]`
69	binder deleted. The proof is mathlib's Stacks 0BFD
70	(`isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`) after observing that
71	`GeometricallyIntegral` is synthesised from the project's four-instance package — a smooth
72	geometrically irreducible scheme over a field is geometrically integral. -/
73	theorem isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField (A : Over (Spec (.of K)))
74	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] :
75	    IsCommMonObj A :=
76	  isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral A
77	
78	/-- **Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.2 over an arbitrary field: a pointed morphism of abelian
79	varieties is a homomorphism.**
80	
81	Same statement as `isMonHom_of_pointed` (`Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`) with the
82	`[IsAlgClosed kbar]` binder deleted.
83	
84	The descent is the one mathlib's 0BFD uses for commutativity, and it works here for the
85	same reason: `IsMonHom` is a *pair of equations*, so a faithful monoidal functor reflects
86	it. Concretely, with `F = Over.pullback (Spec.map (algebraMap K K̄))`:
87	
88	* the abelian-variety package is stable under this base change, so the `k̄` corollary
89	  `isMonHom_of_pointed` applies to `F.map α`;
90	* pointedness transports along `F` (`F.map` of the pointing equation, plus `ε`);
91	* `Over.pullback` is faithful, and `μ`-naturality turns the upstairs `mul_hom` into the
92	  downstairs one after cancelling the (iso) monoidal comparison.
93	
94	No smoothness or properness of `B` beyond what the `k̄` statement asks, and no
95	quasi-projectivity: nothing in the argument is field-specific once the engine is applied
96	upstairs. -/
97	theorem isMonHom_of_pointed_arbitraryField {A B : Over (Spec (.of K))}
98	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
99	    [GrpObj B] [IsProper B.hom]
100	    (α : A ⟶ B) (hα : η[A] ≫ α = η[B]) : IsMonHom α := by
101	  let f := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom <| algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))
102	  let F := Over.pullback f
103	  let A' := F.obj A
104	  let B' := F.obj B
105	  -- the abelian-variety package is stable under this base change
106	  have : IsProper A'.hom := by change IsProper (Limits.pullback.snd A.hom f); infer_instance
107	  have : Smooth A'.hom := by change Smooth (Limits.pullback.snd A.hom f); infer_instance
108	  have : GeometricallyIrreducible A'.hom := by
109	    change GeometricallyIrreducible (Limits.pullback.snd A.hom f); infer_instance
110	  have : IsProper B'.hom := by change IsProper (Limits.pullback.snd B.hom f); infer_instance
111	  -- the `k̄` corollary applies upstairs
112	  have hup : IsMonHom (F.map α) := by
113	    have hpt : η[A'] ≫ F.map α = η[B'] := by simp [← Functor.map_comp, hα]
114	    exact isMonHom_of_pointed (A := A') (B := B') (F.map α) hpt
115	  -- and reflects back down, by faithfulness plus `μ`-naturality
116	  refine { one_hom := hα, mul_hom := ?_ }
117	  exact F.map_injective <| by
118	    simpa [← Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ_natural_assoc,
119	      ← cancel_epi (Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ F A A)] using IsMonHom.mul_hom (F.map α)
120	
121	end AlgebraicGeometry

name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:

/-- **The self-product is geometrically irreducible over `k̄`.** The projection
`pullback.fst A.hom A.hom` is a base change of the geometrically irreducible `A.hom`,
and geometric irreducibility composes (`GeometricallyIrreducible.comp`). -/
theorem geometricallyIrreducible_tensorObj_self (A : Over (Spec (.of kbar)))
    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] : GeometricallyIrreducible (A ⊗ A).hom := by
  rw [Over.tensorObj_hom]
  exact GeometricallyIrreducible.comp (pullback.fst A.hom A.hom) A.hom

/-- **The underlying scheme of the self-product is reduced.** It is smooth over `k̄`
by `smooth_tensorObj_self`, and a scheme smooth over an algebraically closed field is
reduced (`Scheme.isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed`). -/
theorem isReduced_tensorObj_self_left (A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [Smooth A.hom] :
    IsReduced (A ⊗ A).left := by
  haveI := smooth_tensorObj_self A
  exact Scheme.isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed (A ⊗ A)

/-! ## §2. Milne I.1.2 and I.1.4 on the project's standard package

With §1 the two rigidity corollaries apply to an abelian variety carrying only
`[GrpObj] [IsProper] [Smooth] [GeometricallyIrreducible]`. -/

/-- **Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.4 on the standard package — an abelian variety is
commutative.**

Same statement as `isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth`, but with the three self-product
hypotheses discharged by §1, so it applies to any `A` carrying the project's

actual abelian variety, and hence the symmetrisation step of Milne III.6.1
available. -/

    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] :
    IsCommMonObj A := by
  haveI := geometricallyIrreducible_tensorObj_self A
  haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_tensorObj_self A
  haveI := isReduced_tensorObj_self_left A
  exact isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth

/-- **Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.2 on the standard package — a pointed morphism of
abelian varieties is a homomorphism.**

    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
    [GrpObj B] [IsProper B.hom]

  haveI := geometricallyIrreducible_tensorObj_self A
  haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_tensorObj_self A
  haveI := isReduced_tensorObj_self_left A
  exact av_regularMap_isHom_of_zero α hα

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed

something a later session can re-run.

symmetric power is given, uses that `C` is a curve. The genus enters only as the
number `g` of factors. -/

/-- **The Albanese universal property with an arbitrary abelian variety as target.**

Milne Proposition III.6.1 in its widest honest form: for *any* object `C`, any `g`,
any symmetric-power datum `SymPowData C g`, and any two abelian varieties `J`, `A`
over `k̄`, a pointed `φ : C ⟶ A` factors uniquely through a pointed `aj : C ⟶ J` whose
symmetrisation is `f`, given the descent datum.

Axiom-clean. Its role is twofold: it is the reusable statement (nothing about curves
or the Jacobian is needed), and comparing its axiom set with that of
`Pic0.albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData` attributes the latter's `sorryAx`
entirely to the Picard seam. See the section note above. -/
theorem albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData_generic
    {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) (g : ℕ)
    (D : SymPowData C g)
    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g), permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
    {J A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom]
    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A])
    (aj : C ⟶ J) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)
    (hf : letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package J
      D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj)
    (haj0 : P0 ≫ aj = η[J])
    (hdesc : letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
      ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ) :
    ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ := by
  letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package J
  letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
  exact exists_unique_albanese_factorisation D f P0 i₀ hproj aj hf haj0 φ hφ
    (fun ψ hψ => isMonHom_of_pointed ψ hψ) hdesc

6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.AVSelfProduct
8	
9	/-!
10	# The two rigidity corollaries over an arbitrary base field
11	
12	`Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean` proves Milne §I.1 Corollaries 1.4 (an abelian variety is
13	commutative) and 1.2 (a pointed morphism of abelian varieties is a homomorphism) on the
14	project's four-instance abelian-variety package, but over an **algebraically closed**
15	field: both rest on `RigidityLemma.lean`, whose engine binds `[IsAlgClosed kbar]`.
16	
17	This file removes that binder. Both corollaries hold over an arbitrary field `K`.
18	
19	## Why this matters, and what it does not buy
20	
21	The headline `picardJacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) is stated over an arbitrary field
22	with no rational-point hypothesis (owner decision, protection `I-0491`). Its fifth
23	obligation `isAlbanese_pic0Et` is the Albanese universal property there, and its docstring
24	prices the passage from `k̄` to `k` as "the Galois-descent step of cluster `G`".
25	
26	That price is too high for *this* part of the passage. The Albanese engine
27	(`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`) is already field-agnostic — it lives in an arbitrary
28	`CartesianMonoidalCategory` — and consumes exactly two geometric inputs, the two rigidity
29	corollaries. Both are available over `K`:
30	
31	* commutativity is *already* in mathlib over an arbitrary field
32	  (`isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`, Stacks 0BFD), which descends it
33	  from `K̄` internally; the project's own `IsAlgClosed` version is not needed at that
34	  strength, because `GeometricallyIntegral` synthesises from the four-instance package;
35	* pointed rigidity descends by the *same* argument, which is what this file supplies
36	  (`isMonHom_of_pointed_arbitraryField`). `IsMonHom` is a pair of equations, `Over.pullback`
37	  along `K → K̄` is faithful and monoidal, and the abelian-variety package is stable under
38	  that base change — so the `k̄` corollary applies upstairs and reflects back down.
39	
40	**What is still owed for `isAlbanese_pic0Et`, and this file does not touch any of it:**
41	the symmetric power `Sym^g C` (equivalently `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)`), Milne III.5.1(a)
42	birationality as a section over a dense open, the genus-`0` case, the basepoint condition,
43	and the transport of the Abel–Jacobi morphism to `Pic0SchemeEt`. Nothing here is a discharge
44	of the headline sorry; what it does is establish that the *field* is not among the reasons
45	that sorry is open.
46	
47	## Main results
48	
49	* `isMonHom_of_pointed_arbitraryField` — Milne I.1.2 over an arbitrary field.
50	* `isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField` — Milne I.1.4 over an arbitrary field, recorded
51	  here so the pair is available together (the proof is mathlib's 0BFD plus one instance).
52	-/
53	
54	set_option autoImplicit false
55	
56	universe u
57	
58	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
59	open scoped CategoryTheory.Obj
60	
61	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
62	
63	variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
64	
65	/-- **Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.4 over an arbitrary field: an abelian variety is
66	commutative.**
67	
68	Same conclusion as `isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package` with the `[IsAlgClosed]`
69	binder deleted. The proof is mathlib's Stacks 0BFD
70	(`isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`) after observing that
71	`GeometricallyIntegral` is synthesised from the project's four-instance package — a smooth
72	geometrically irreducible scheme over a field is geometrically integral. -/
73	theorem isCommMonObj_of_package_arbitraryField (A : Over (Spec (.of K)))
74	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] :
75	    IsCommMonObj A :=
76	  isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral A
77	
78	/-- **Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.2 over an arbitrary field: a pointed morphism of abelian
79	varieties is a homomorphism.**
80	
81	Same statement as `isMonHom_of_pointed` (`Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`) with the
82	`[IsAlgClosed kbar]` binder deleted.
83	
84	The descent is the one mathlib's 0BFD uses for commutativity, and it works here for the
85	same reason: `IsMonHom` is a *pair of equations*, so a faithful monoidal functor reflects
86	it. Concretely, with `F = Over.pullback (Spec.map (algebraMap K K̄))`:
87	
88	* the abelian-variety package is stable under this base change, so the `k̄` corollary
89	  `isMonHom_of_pointed` applies to `F.map α`;
90	* pointedness transports along `F` (`F.map` of the pointing equation, plus `ε`);
91	* `Over.pullback` is faithful, and `μ`-naturality turns the upstairs `mul_hom` into the
92	  downstairs one after cancelling the (iso) monoidal comparison.
93	
94	No smoothness or properness of `B` beyond what the `k̄` statement asks, and no
95	quasi-projectivity: nothing in the argument is field-specific once the engine is applied
96	upstairs. -/
97	theorem isMonHom_of_pointed_arbitraryField {A B : Over (Spec (.of K))}
98	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
99	    [GrpObj B] [IsProper B.hom]
100	    (α : A ⟶ B) (hα : η[A] ≫ α = η[B]) : IsMonHom α := by
101	  let f := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom <| algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))
102	  let F := Over.pullback f
103	  let A' := F.obj A

An object `J` (with abelian-variety structure) is the Albanese of `(C, P)` if it
receives a universal pointed morphism `C ⟶ J` sending `P` to the identity. -/
def IsAlbanese (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
    (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] : Prop :=
  ∃ α : C ⟶ J, P ≫ α = η[J] ∧
    ∀ {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom]
      [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (_ : P ≫ f = η[A]),
      ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = α ≫ g

namespace IsAlbanese

noncomputable def ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) : C ⟶ J :=
  Classical.choose h

lemma comp_ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) :
    P ≫ h.ofCurve = η[J] :=
  (Classical.choose_spec h).1

lemma exists_unique_ofCurve_comp {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J)
    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
    ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = h.ofCurve ≫ g :=
  (Classical.choose_spec h).2 f hf

/-- The Albanese object is unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the
universal morphisms. -/
theorem unique {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C}
